name: Mlomp
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists/sociolinguistic surveys (Barry 1987 subgrouping; Carlton & Rand 1993/1994); no phonology or grammar of Mlomp exists

sources.citation: Sambou, Anne Mireille Thérèse. 2021. Morphosyntaxe du kunoofaay (jóola de Mlomp Nord), langue atlantique du Sénégal. PhD thesis, Universität zu Köln (KUPS 53822). 362 pp.
sources.note: Ch. 2 Phonologie (pp. 12-26) covers consonants, 10 vowels (+/-ATR, acute accent marks +ATR only: p. 20 'les cinq voyelles tendues (+ATR) portent un accent aigu'), vowel length minimal pairs, syllable types (C)V(V)(C)(N)(C) and syllable combinations; no section or sentence on word stress, accent or tone anywhere in the thesis (grep accent/ton/prosod/suprasegm: only intonation/pause remarks in the focus chapter).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) Mlomp language; Wikipédia (fr) Mlomp (langue); Ethnologue 22nd ed. profile (2019 Wayback capture)
sources.note: Identity only: Mlomp/Gulompaay/Mlomp North, village of Mlomp north of the Casamance river 25 km west of Bignona between Tendouck and Thiobon, closest to Karon; not the Mlomp near Oussouye where Kasa is spoken. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Carlton, Elizabeth Masland & Sharon R. Rand. 1994. Compilation de listes de mots Swadesh modifiées recueillies parmi les langues du groupe diola (sud du Sénégal). Journal of West African Languages 24(2): 85-119.
sources.note: Scan without text layer (scanned at 200 dpi). Two-page introduction plus phone charts (Fig. 3 consonants p. 88, Fig. 4 vowels p. 89) and 170-item phonetic wordlists for 31 villages incl. MLN = M'Lomp (nord) buluf; nothing on stress, and the transcriptions carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid mlom1238 (page, JSON and md.ini) and hh.bib entries with lgcode Mlomp [mlo]
sources.note: Sources listed: Barry 1987 (MED, wordlist_or_less), Carlton & Rand 1993, 1994, plus Ethnologue/ELCat/UNESCO records; no grammar, phonology or sketch listed; Sambou 2021 is absent from Glottolog.

sources.citation: Badji, Ibrahima. 2007. La détermination nominale en Mlomp. Mémoire de DEA de Linguistique, Université Cheikh Anta Diop, Dakar.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Second Mlomp-specific study; noun determination, so unlikely to state stress, but its introduction may summarize Badji 2006 phonology.

sources.citation: Badji, Ibrahima. 2006. Phonologie et règles morphophonologiques dans la formation du nom simple en diola Mlomp (Rive droite Casamance). Mémoire de Maîtrise de Linguistique, Université Cheikh Anta Diop, Dakar.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of the language (Sambou 2021: 12 says it presented the phonology 'largement'); a UCAD maîtrise phonology normally has a suprasegmental section and is the most likely place for a stress statement.

sources.citation: Carlton, Elizabeth Masland & Sharon R. Rand. 1993. Enquête sociolinguistique sur les langues Diolas de basse Casamance. Cahiers de recherche linguistique 2. Dakar: SIL.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: SIL survey with intelligibility data and orthographic conventions across Jóola varieties; small chance of a remark on accent in the transcription notes; sil.org blocked from our machine.

sources.citation: Barry, Abdoulaye. 1987. The Joola Languages: Subgrouping and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of London (SOAS). 345 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Comparative thesis with wordlists and phonological sketches of 22 Jóola varieties incl. Gulompaay (Gp); may contain a general statement on Jóola stress/accent applicable to Mlomp; Glottolog's MED for the language.

sources.citation: Pozdniakov, Konstantin & Guillaume Segerer. 2024. A genealogical classification of Atlantic languages. In F. Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford Guide to the Atlantic Languages of West Africa. OUP. (HAL halshs-01671284)
